cases.hint: reject high-s; do not normalize on receipt
cases.name: suite2_high_s_twin_refused
cases.why: ECDSA admits (r, n-s) as an equally valid signature. Accepting both would give one message two valid encodings and diverge the transcript hash, so the high-s form is refused rather than normalized.

cases.hint: check the SEC1 tag explicitly rather than delegating to the parser
cases.name: suite2_pubkey_tag_0x04_refused
cases.why: exactly one public key encoding is legal (compressed, 33 bytes). Common parsers accept 0x05 by reading y-parity from the low bit, yielding the same key as 0x03 — a second encoding of one key is a second canonical object and a second hash.
